headline_marked: Home Minister: [[IGP's crossfire remarks were wrong]]
headline: Home Minister: IGP's crossfire remarks were wrong
summary: Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated the government has 'zero tolerance' for extrajudicial killings and deaths in police custody.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has criticized the Inspector General of Police (IGP) for remarks regarding 'crossfires,' stating that the comments were not appropriate.
In a post on his verified Facebook page on Tuesday night, the Minister clarified that the government does not want crossfires and maintains a 'zero tolerance' policy toward them.
He noted that the IGP had spoken carelessly and that such statements were neither right nor appropriate for the situation.
The Minister emphasized that the government will not tolerate extrajudicial killings or deaths occurring while suspects are in police custody.
He further stated that establishing the rule of law and improving law and order are the primary priorities of the current government.
caption:
The government has 'zero tolerance' for extrajudicial killings. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says the IGP's comments on crossfire were 'wrong'.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has criticized the Inspector General of Police (IGP) for remarks regarding 'crossfires,' stating that the comments were not appropriate.

In a post on his verified Facebook page on Tuesday night, the Minister clarified that the government does not want crossfires and maintains a 'zero tolerance' policy toward them.

He noted that the IGP had spoken carelessly and that such statements were neither right nor appropriate for the situation.

The Minister emphasized that the government will not tolerate extrajudicial killings or deaths occurring while suspects are in police custody.

He further stated that establishing the rule of law and improving law and order are the primary priorities of the current government.

#Bangladesh #LawAndOrder #HumanRights #Police #Government

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com
